teams.heading: Fiji pitch pride over money in bid to lure Mark Nawaqanitawase
teams.body: Fiji are pitching pride over money in their bid to lure Mark Nawaqanitawase, according to Reuters. Planet Rugby reports that Fiji have broken their silence on the player's possible shock defection. The pitch came the day before Jake White's first Test in charge, a 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo, and ahead of November's Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: A new Fiji-side story about pursuing a player, not yet run, with Fiji's stake clear in the headline.

teams.heading: Bristol's Harry Randall says he 'can't pick' himself for England squad
teams.body: Bristol Bears scrum-half Harry Randall, 28, wants back into the England squad, telling the club website: "I'd love to get back in the England squad. I'd love to go to a World Cup. But, ultimately, I can't pick myself." Planet Rugby reports he is unlikely to make the upcoming Nations Championship squad, with Jack van Poortvliet, Ben Spencer, Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland all ahead of him in the pecking order. Bears director of rugby Pat Lam says Randall is in the "form of his life".

lead.why: A new men's England selection story from the squad picture, with a player quoted directly, and it avoids the already-run Van Poortvliet item and the women's Canada result.

teams.heading: France referee boss challenges World Rugby over hip-drop tackle ban
teams.body: France's referee boss has challenged World Rugby over the hip-drop tackle ban, according to the latest coverage, which also reports the governing body banning two dangerous tackle types in a player welfare move. Earlier reports had a referee boss accusing World Rugby of breaking an agreement as both sides sought clarity on the new laws. The final wording is still to be agreed between World Rugby and referee associations.

teams.heading: London Irish club target Championship return next season under Steve Daniels
teams.body: London Irish, the club inactive since going into administration in June 2023, hope to return to professional rugby as early as next season. New owner and chairman Steve Daniels has vowed to put the club "firmly back on the rugby map" after Gamechanger Investments bought the name, brand and intellectual property from Kyle Jordan and Daniel McKeown. Chief executive Jamie Balls says the club would like to join the Championship at the earliest opportunity and would otherwise wait another year.

lead.why: The only item in the shortlist that is new, men's and not already run; the national-team items are either a repeat or women's.

teams.heading: Italy suffer fourth straight defeat, winning one of last five
teams.body: Italy are on a run of four straight defeats. In their last five games they have won one and lost four, with the sequence reading most recent first as L L L L W. The most recent game was a 57-10 loss away to Australia in July, in the Nations Championship group stage. South Africa are next up.

teams.heading: Scotland climb world rankings without playing ahead of Nations Championship
teams.body: Scotland have climbed the world rankings without playing a match, a move reported by MSN ahead of the Nations Championship. The side have played three games in the competition, sitting five of 12 in the log with two wins and one defeat. The last result was a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round three, and the next assignment is a Round four meeting with New Zealand.

lead.why: It is the only current men's national-team item in the shortlist that has not already been run; the squad story was run today and the others concern a retired player or older events.

teams.heading: Freddie Thomas, left out of Wales squad, scores decisive try for Gloucester
teams.body: At Kingsholm, Gloucester beat Bath 23-5 in a Gallagher Premiership derby, and Freddie Thomas scored a decisive try with 18 tackles and 18 carries. The 24-year-old has played mostly blindside flanker this season rather than lock, and was left out of Steve Tandy's latest Wales squad. Gloucester are top of the Gallagher Prem, and Wales centre Max Llewellyn also crossed for the winners.

lead.why: It is a new item that puts a Wales selection question on a player outside the Faletau story already run today.

teams.heading: Argentina drew 28-28 with Australia in September, one win in last five
teams.body: Argentina's most recent game was a 28-28 draw with Australia at home in September, an International Friendlies fixture. In their last five games they have won one, lost three and drawn one, most recent first: draw, loss, loss, loss, win. Going into the weekend, the log has them eighth of 12, with three played, one won and two lost. Their next match is Ireland, in Round four of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Teddy Wilson earns Wallabies call-up as son of 1999 World Cup winner
teams.body: Scrum-half Teddy Wilson has been named in Les Kiss' 33-man squad for the November Nations Championship Tests, with prop Tom Lambert one of the two new faces. Wilson is the son of David Wilson, who won 79 caps and was in the 1999 World Cup-winning side. The Guardian reports Wilson will push Tate McDermott for back-up to Ryan Lonergan, who has established himself as the standout No. 9. Wilson says his father "just lets me play my game".

lead.why: A debutant's call-up with a famous World Cup-winning father is a distinct angle from the returning-players story already run today.

teams.heading: Japan's centenary Test slips 34-28 to Fiji as Volavola's late penalties decide
teams.body: Japan's centenary celebrations in Tokyo ended with a 34-28 defeat to Fiji, who avenged their Pacific Nations Cup final loss to the Brave Blossoms. The sides were level at 21-all at half-time, with both teams scoring three converted tries. Fiji retook the lead through Terio Tamani's 44th-minute try, and Japan levelled at 28-all before veteran Ben Volavola kicked two penalties in the 60th and 69th minutes.

lead.why: It is the fresh men's Test result from Japan's centenary match, and the only men's national-team item in the shortlist.

teams.heading: Shannon Frizell, Tyrel Lomax and Samisoni Taukei’aho ruled out of Europe tour
teams.body: Frizell ruptured the posterior cruciate ligament in his left knee and faces six weeks out, while Taukei’aho is expected to miss four to six weeks with a torn calf muscle. Prop Lomax, troubled by a neck disc injury since Super Rugby, will stay in New Zealand for treatment. The trio were ruled out after the second Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney; Richie Mo’unga, who missed both Bledisloe Tests with a calf tear, is not yet ruled out of the tour, SA Rugby Magazine reports.

lead.why: A fresh, specific injury update on three named All Blacks, with the detail of each layoff, ahead of the Europe tour.

teams.heading: Cheslin Kolbe explains why he came home to Stormers after Japan
teams.body: Cheslin Kolbe has explained why he came back to South Africa after nine years abroad. He told the For the Love of Rugby podcast he had missed his wife and children, who stayed in South Africa while he played in Japan. "I've been wanting to come home for so long, but I'm a firm believer that God will put us where he wants us to be at the right time," he said. His Stormers debut has been delayed after he broke his jaw on Springbok duty.

lead.why: A Springbok winger explaining his return home to the Stormers is a current squad story, and it is new since the last edition.
